description_under_test: The V1 GitHub Data Quality Gate — a live-Postgres-backed semantic schema and data-profile check that runs as a distinct required CI status check (data-quality-gate), DISTINCT from the sibling data-standards skill's static textual DDL checks.
source: V1 build (2026-09-02): scope detector + Postgres introspection + schema-diff classifier + contract/naming gate + data-profile gate + developer-evidence exception + own Slack notifier + durable audit trail. Trigger cases follow the pack's established evals.json convention (see skills/data-standards/evals/evals.json). Correctness cases split into pure-logic (no Postgres, run anywhere) and integration (needs a real reachable Postgres — see tests/test_gate_integration.py, which self-skips rather than fails when none is available).
method: Trigger cases: run each query in a fresh session 3x; a should_trigger case passes above a 0.5 trigger rate, a should_not case passes below it — should_not cases here specifically probe confusion with the sibling data-standards skill, since the two are easy to conflate by name. Correctness cases: run the named unittest module/class and check it passes (or, for integration cases, passes when Postgres is reachable and self-skips cleanly when it isn't).

cases.query: add a live-database schema validation gate that actually queries Postgres
check if this constraint actually exists in the real database, not just the migration text
block a migration that would truncate real production data
profile the data quality of this table before we merge
why did the data-quality-gate check fail on my PR?

does this migration meet our data standards?

how many teachers used Rumi last week?
post an update to Slack about the deploy
write an implementation plan for the new feature
check my git commit message formatting

correctness_cases.expect_result: all tests pass — compliant additions pass, removed table/column blocks, narrowing/truncating blocks, PK/FK/unique/check weakening blocks, undeclared rename never suppressed
all tests pass — malformed table contract, data-profile.yaml, and change.yaml each raise ConfigError; no-contract and disabled-template files are skipped correctly
all tests pass — new unclassified PII-shaped column blocks, declared sensitivity clears it, everything else advisory-only
all tests pass — deterministic tolerance/IQR/robust-z/PSI checks, zero LLM/opaque-score involvement
all tests pass — matching evidence passes, mismatched before/after fails, partial coverage leaves remainder blocking
all tests pass — malformed scope.json exits 2, irrelevant files report NOT applicable, exclude wins over include
all tests pass — no path/credential ever survives sanitize(); never-block guarantee on missing channel config
all tests pass — composite-FK row grouping produces correct positional pairs (regression test for the cartesian-product bug found and fixed during build), DSN redaction never leaks a password

when a real Postgres is reachable (DATA_QUALITY_GATE_TEST_DSN, or in CI's own service containers): compliant addition passes, widening passes, dropped column blocks, narrowed column blocks, unreachable head DB fails closed with ERROR. When no Postgres is reachable: all 7 tests report skipped, never a failure.

all tests pass — SQL type keywords translate to the same udt_name vocabulary introspect.py's live snapshot produces (VARCHAR(255)->varchar/255, NUMERIC(10,2)->numeric/10/2, DOUBLE PRECISION->float8, SERIAL->int4), inline and table-level (including composite) PRIMARY KEY are both detected correctly, and the resulting snapshot dict is directly consumable by schema_diff.py's and contract_check.py's real functions — proven by feeding parser output straight into diff_columns()/check_new_table() rather than only asserting on the snapshot's shape in isolation.

correctness_cases.command: echo '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"scratch.sql","content":"CREATE TABLE audit_events (event_type TEXT NOT NULL);"}}' | python3 hooks/live-schema-shape-gate.py
correctness_cases.why_it_matters: The schema-shape half of this gate (contract_check.py's check_new_table) must block live, the instant a new table with no PRIMARY KEY is written — mirrors data-standards' own live-edit hook's D1 case, one enforcement layer earlier than CI.

correctness_cases.command: echo '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"scratch.sql","content":"CREATE TABLE broadcast_logs (id UUID PRIMARY KEY, admin_ip_address VARCHAR(45));"}}' | python3 hooks/live-schema-shape-gate.py
correctness_cases.why_it_matters: Proves the hook loads a REAL table contract from the target repo's own .data-quality-gate/table-contracts/ (not a synthetic fixture) and correctly flags admin_ip_address as PII-shaped with no sensitivity classification declared — the exact contract this pack ships for its own fork-test coverage.

correctness_cases.command: echo '{"tool_name":"Write",..."content":"CREATE TABLE broadcast_logs (id UUID PRIMARY KEY, unexpected_new_col TEXT);"}}' | python3 hooks/live-schema-shape-gate.py
correctness_cases.why_it_matters: column_not_in_contract (and type_mismatch_vs_contract / nullability_mismatch_vs_contract) are advisory-only per contract_check.py's own contract (blocking: False) — this case caught a REAL bug during development where the hook forwarded every finding as blocking regardless of that flag, which would have made an unrelated advisory note refuse an otherwise-compliant edit. Fixed by filtering to blocking-only findings before deciding to exit 2.

correctness_cases.fixture: a scratch git repo with migrations/users.sql committed to main, phone VARCHAR(20)
correctness_cases.command: an Edit narrowing phone to VARCHAR(10) via hooks/live-schema-shape-gate.py, run from inside that repo
correctness_cases.why_it_matters: Per explicit instruction, "before" for this live diff is the target repo's default branch (origin/HEAD if resolvable, else local main), read via `git show <ref>:<path>` — not a live database. This proves the full path works: resolving the ref, reading the committed file, parsing it, diffing it against the Edit's prospective content, and correctly classifying the length-20-to-10 change as NARROWED/blocking. A widen to VARCHAR(40) against the same committed baseline correctly does NOT block (WIDENED, non-blocking).

correctness_cases.fixture: the C14 scratch repo, with TALEEMABAD_DATA_STANDARDS_BYPASS exported first
correctness_cases.command: export TALEEMABAD_DATA_STANDARDS_BYPASS="<a real reason>"; re-run C14's narrowing Edit through hooks/live-schema-shape-gate.py; separately, re-run with a generic reason like "bypass"
correctness_cases.expect: a validated reason: exit 0, a record appended to .data-standards-bypass-log.jsonl (the SAME file data-standards' own live hook writes to) with the correct bypassed finding kind and the real commit SHA; a generic/rejected reason: falls through and still blocks (exit 2)
correctness_cases.why_it_matters: This gate deliberately reuses data-standards' bypass variable and bypass_audit.py rather than inventing a second bypass mechanism — per this pack's one-audit-trail principle. The Slack notification for a block/bypass still goes through THIS gate's own notify.py (its own channel, its own 'block' event template) — only the bypass mechanism itself is shared, not the notification path.
